value.rationale: For symmetric eigenvalue problems ordinary Ritz values lie in the true interval, making the failure probability under randomized approximate orthogonality a natural stability question. The sharp orientation-dependent bound (including both the universal half-escape barrier and exponentially small balanced regime) provides a motivated finite-dimensional risk benchmark and distinguishes near-eigenvector worst-case probability from vanishing absolute error. It does not pretend to cover multistep or embedding-conditioned solvers.
